As with the outrageous Aston Martin Valkyrie , the Valhalla is a race car for the road, drawing inspiration from Formula 1 and utilizing lightweight materials and active aerodynamics. The Aston's exterior boasts an exaggerated version of the company's trademark grille along with slippery bodywork. Its central tub is composed of carbon fiber, and the Valhalla's exotic nature is accentuated by dihedral doors. Power comes from a Mercedes-AMG –sourced twin-turbo V-8, mated to a plug-in hybrid system that generates a combined 1064 horsepower. The gas engine feeds power to the rear tires, while the front tires are powered by a pair of electric motors. Aston estimates a top speed of 217 mph, and we think the Valhalla will get to 60 mph in the low-2.0-second range. The Valhalla also has an EV mode, which is good for around 6 miles of all-electric range.

The Valhalla is a new model in Aston Martin's lineup, and it reaches the U.S. as a 2026 model.

When you're buying a multi-million-dollar hypercar like a Bugatti Mistral , there are countless options to choose from even before you start getting into the really bespoke stuff . Selecting your paint shade, upholstery scheme, wheel design and stitching color is just the tip of the iceberg — for instance, on the Mistral, you can replace the elephant sculpture in the shifter with something else, like a mini Statue of Liberty or a screw from a 100-year-old Bugatti, as two customers have done.

There is one option that only a tiny handful of Bugatti owners have gone for, and it's a real shame: the polished engine covers. Almost every modern Bugatti since the Veyron has had their engine bays exposed to the elements, and many buyers get the W16's engine covers painted in a matching or contrasting color, or maybe one of a dozen carbon-fiber finishes, instead of the regular gunmetal. The polished aluminum option is very expensive, but that's not what deters Bugatti customers from optioning it. No, they're just too wimpy.

item.dc:creator: Tyler Brooks
item.description: In a hilariously ironic turn of events, Okaloosa County, Florida , sank the SS United States to the bottom of the Gulf of Mexico on Veteran's Day, turning it into the world's largest artificial reef to provide shelter for local marine life in the wake of human-caused coral reef decimation in the area.

Briefing: In a hilariously ironic turn of events, Okaloosa County, Florida , sank the SS United States to the bottom of the Gulf of Mexico on Veteran's Day, turning it into the world's largest artificial reef to provide shelter for local marine life in the wake of human-caused coral reef decimation in the area.

In a hilariously ironic turn of events, Okaloosa County, Florida , sank the SS United States to the bottom of the Gulf of Mexico on Veteran's Day, turning it into the world's largest artificial reef to provide shelter for local marine life in the wake of human-caused coral reef decimation in the area. The SS United States is longer than the Titanic , measuring 990 feet from bow to stern and 17 stories in height. It was once the fastest ocean liner in the world, known for carrying royalty and celebrities between the U.S. and Europe from its maiden voyage in 1952 to its retirement in 1969.

It actually still holds the record for the world's fastest trans-Atlantic ocean liner, accomplishing the trek in 3 days, 10 hours, and 40 minutes at an average speed of 35.59 knots, and it achieved top speeds of over 38.3 knots, or 44 mph, during trials. This serves as a reminder that even once-great nations — er, ships — can find themselves fallen so far from their former glory that they are better off being totally gutted and sank to the bottom of the ocean rather than wasting time and resources attempting to resuscitate them only for them to still be outdated and irrelevant in a modern world.

The move is effective immediately, according to Stellantis, and Kuniskis — who joined the company in 1992 — will report directly to Pablo Di Si, the automaker's newly promoted North American COO. A European fertiliser manufacturer buys ammonia. Its immediate concern is getting the right product, at the right quality and price, with reliable deliveries. The manufacturer may produce ammonia using hydrogen made on its own site, buy hydrogen through a pipeline, or import ammonia made somewhere else. The last choice preserves much of the downstream industrial work but creates no demand for additional hydrogen production or pipelines inside Europe. That distinction belongs at the start of Europe’s hydrogen strategy.

The European Commission has reopened the strategy for consultation, with submissions due November 23. The Commission acknowledges that renewable and low-carbon hydrogen production and use have grown more slowly than expected. Europe’s public investment decisions now need a closer look at the industries expected to use hydrogen, the products they make, and the routes by which those products can be supplied competitively. The consultation is open until November 23, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Briefing: Normally, it’s easy to identify an incumbent. Establishment figures tend to enjoy advantages—experience, name recognition, resources—that are scarce for upstarts. But in the case of the 2027 Rivian R2 and the 2026 Jeep Recon Moab, it’s hard to say who’s the incumbent and who’s the challenger.

Normally, it’s easy to identify an incumbent. Establishment figures tend to enjoy advantages—experience, name recognition, resources—that are scarce for upstarts. But in the case of the 2027 Rivian R2 and the 2026 Jeep Recon Moab, it’s hard to say who’s the incumbent and who’s the challenger. Jeep has been building SUVs since the 1940s, as it’s happy to constantly remind you, but is relatively new to EVs. Meanwhile, the first Rivians hit the road just five years ago, but EVs are all that it builds, and the R2 is the brand’s third model. Which incumbency is more advantageous? Let’s take a look.

The fresh-out-of-the-oven R2 hews to the typical launch strategy of offering the most expensive version first. Thus, our 2027 model is a Performance trim with the Launch package, which brings a 4400-pound tow rating and hands-free driving assist. Simpler variants are coming soon, priced closer to 50 grand, but our tester with its $2000 Launch Green paint tallied $61,485. Happily, the R2’s most delightful feature, its power roll-down hatch glass, is standard. Sorry, Toyota 4Runner , Rivian is onto the lifestyle appeal of a dropped rear window with a surfboard poking out. Or a dog or two who won’t be breathing exhaust fumes.

Planning a family road trip usually starts with excitement. Everyone gets involved in choosing the destination, checking the route, preparing snacks, and packing luggage for the journey. Parents make sure the kids have entertainment, while other family members prepare drinks, travel essentials, and everything needed for a comfortable ride. However, amid all the preparation, some easily overlooked vehicle interior problems can turn into unexpected inconveniences along the way. A little mud brought into the cabin, difficulty climbing into a tall pickup, or small belongings scattered across the seats may not seem like serious issues before departure. Yet after several hours on the road, these minor problems can become frustrating, particularly when traveling with children or older family members. A comfortable road trip is not only about reaching the destination; it is also about making sure everyone can enjoy the journey without constantly dealing with unnecessary mess and discomfort.

Family travel puts a vehicle’s interior to the test. One of the most common challenges is keeping the floor clean. Children may step into the vehicle with muddy shoes after outdoor activities, while food crumbs, spilled drinks, and snack wrappers can quickly make the factory carpet look messy. Cleaning these stains can take time, especially after a long trip. Another issue is getting in and out of taller SUVs and pickup trucks. Although their higher ground clearance is useful for different driving conditions, the height can make entry and exit less convenient for young children and older passengers. Repeatedly climbing into the cabin may require extra effort and assistance. Finally, there is the problem of small items getting everywhere. Toys, charging cables, tissues, water bottles, and travel accessories often end up under seats or scattered around the cabin. When passengers cannot find what they need, the journey can become less organized. These problems may be ordinary, but addressing them before departure can make a noticeable difference to the overall travel experience.

On Tuesday, BYD announced that it will combine clean solar power, its proprietary Flash Charging tech that uses local energy storage, and robotic arms into one EV charging system.

The core of this system is BYD's Flash Charging, which draws power from the grid like any other EV charging station. Unlike others, though, it stores the electricity in two on-site 185-kilowatt batteries. That stored energy can then be pumped into your EV way quicker than it would be if it were drawing from the grid directly, BYD says.

Now our spies have gotten a better look at the test mule, and I know exactly what it is: This is an early prototype for the new Scouts .

Somehow, I don't think I saw a single comment online thinking that it was a Scout mule based on the Reddit photos, but that's definitely what it is. This time, it wasn't spied in Moab but at a secret Audi test facility in Germany, which is one of the few giveaways as to its identity — another obvious one being the tow hooks. I've already been surprised that Scout test mules haven't been regularly spied by now, since just this week Scout announced that it's starting to construct "validation builds" at its factory in newly blue South Carolina, and prototypes with closer-to-production bodies have apparently already been out there for months. This one is likely an older mule that's still out there racking up test miles, which is probably fine since since the Scouts have been delayed so much .

These days we're used to the United Arab Emirates' police forces showing off the latest and greatest sportscar and supercar additions to their fleet. Just this year, Dubai Police welcomed a modified Lamborghini Temerario and Ferrari 812 Superfast with tweaks from Mansory. And for the emirate of Abu Dhabi, we've seen them champion cars like a Lykan Hypersport and Nissan GT-R in the past. These headline-grabbing supercars are more often than not an element of public outreach campaigns and PR stunts.

But the first sports car, a Porsche 924, to join the UAE's federal police fleet was an active service vehicle, used to escort Queen Elizabeth II on her first royal visit to the UAE in 1979. Over the years, the 924 has remained in the UAE Federal Police Fleet, and has been seen in various colors. But for its recent extensive restoration, it was decided that the original livery from nearly 50 years ago was only fitting.
